args.body:
Hi Dora! I just had a look at your personal website at www.dora-website.com and wanted to share some feedback.

What works:
- It's clean and loads instantly — no clutter, no pop-ups, no autoplay. That's a good foundation.
- The contact email is right there on the page, so it's easy to reach you.

What could be better:
- The site is currently just one line of text, so there's not much to explore. A personal site is a great chance to show who you are — a short intro, a few photos, or a list of your projects and interests would give visitors something to come back for.
- Consider adding a few sections: an "About" blurb, a portfolio or projects page, and maybe a small blog or notes section.
- A bit of visual design would help too — even a simple layout with headings and images makes a small amount of content feel much more polished.
- If you do add more pages, a simple navigation menu or links at the top would make it easy to browse.

Overall it's a nice, tidy starting point — it just needs a little more content and personality to really shine. Nice work getting it live!

Best,
Emma Johnson

Hi Eve! I visited your blog at www.eve-blog.com and wanted to share some feedback.

What works:
- The site is simple and fast, with a clear introduction that immediately tells visitors what it's about.
- I loved learning that hiking is your favorite hobby — that's a great theme to build a blog around, and it gives readers an instant sense of who you are.

What could be better:
- Right now the homepage doesn't show any actual posts. For a blog, the most valuable thing is letting readers see your latest writing at a glance — a list of recent posts with titles, dates, and short summaries would make the front page much more useful.
- Since hiking is your passion, adding a few photos from your trails, plus tags or categories (e.g. "Trip Reports," "Gear," "Trail Tips"), would make it easy for readers to find what they like.
- An "About" page and a way to subscribe to new posts (RSS or an email signup) would help turn casual visitors into regulars.
- A little visual polish — a header image, consistent typography, and readable post layouts — would make the writing feel more inviting.

Overall, a solid foundation with a clear voice. With a few posts and some structure, it could become a really enjoyable blog to follow. Keep up the good work!

Best,
Emma Johnson
